newsitem.title: GERMANY: German J.Walter Thompson reports record 96 sales.
newsitem.headline: German J.Walter Thompson reports record 96 sales.

text.p: Advertising agency J. Walter Thompson's German unit on Friday posted record 1996 sales and predicted more growth this year, as last year's success in wooing new clients should show a positive knock-on effect.

J. Walter Thompson GmbH, boasting accounts for carmaker Mazda and photo group Kodak, said 1996 turnover rose by 7.4 percent to 85 million marks while billings climbed by 7.6 percent to 566 million marks.

New clients Deutsche Shell, Mazda and Kodak along with existing clients Kellogg, de Beers and Rolex helped J. Walter Thompson GmbH move ahead one spot to become Germany's seventh largest advertising agency.
Group officials predicted growth in J. Walter Thompson GmbH's client base would continue to propel sales this year.
"We are also quite confident for 1997 because part of these profits will not even affect our books until this year," said Ulrich Rohrbach, a manager at the Frankfurt-based agency.

Strong 1996 sales helped the agency increase its workforce by 6 percent to 386 employees, including employees at the agency's subsidiaries Effective Media, marketing agency T&A and Basisresearch, a market research institute.
The parent company's eastern European regional agencies, managed by the German unit, expanded dramatically in 1996, posting a 30 percent rise in turnover to 18 million marks.
J. Walter Thompson, which operates 29 agencies in Europe, is owned by WPP, the world's largest marketing and advertising services group.

Personnel changes are planned at the German unit with Peter Erzberger slated to replace Michael Maedel in July, after Maedel moved to the parent agency in London. Erzberger was previously with Scholz & Friends in Hamburg.
Joe Nutt, head of the Frankfurt office, is expected to move to the Hamburg office to oversee that office's expansion during the summer.
